newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovene banks SKB and UBK seal merger.
newsitem.headline: Slovene banks SKB and UBK seal merger.

text.p: Slovenia's second biggest bank SKB sealed a merger with smaller rival UBK on Monday when the two signed an agreement to create a single banking group from July 1.
In a joint statement, the two confirmed SKB would buy 51 percent of UBK, taking control of investment and private banking. UBK would remain active in small business banking.
"Our experience so far has shown that the concept of an all-round bank is very expensive for a small bank ... and that specialisation is a good alternative," UBK said in a statement.
In May the banks announced SKB would buy UBK's portfolio, with a value of 340 million tolars ($2.1 million), and shares worth 160 billion tolars. They did not reveal the purchase price.
SKB is Slovenia's second largest bank with balance sheet assets of 208.3 billion tolars at the end of last year.

UBK is among the smallest of the country's 28 banks, with a market share of less than one percent and balance sheet assets of 13.2 billion. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439 ($ = 158.6 Slovenian Tolars)
